The petitioner is seeking compensation in the wake of Detailed Accident Report(DAR) filed by police corresponding to the investigation carried out in case FIR No. 161/19 U/s 279/337 IPC registered at PS. K.N.K. Marg with regard to Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 28.04.2019 at about 11:15 am at K.N.K. Marg, near M.C. Primary School, Dwarkadhish, Delhi,

sentences.text: DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
2. According to DAR, on 28.04.2019 the petitioner was going to his work place on his motorcycle bearing no. DL1SS2953.

At about 11:15AM, when he reached at main K.N.K. Marg, near North NDMC Primary School Road, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver(respondent no.
1) at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner came and hit against his motorcycle, as a result of which, he alongwith his motorcycle fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He was taken to BSA Hospital, Rohini, Delhi, where he was MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS.
K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 medically examined.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and the same was found uninsured during the period in question.

3. In their joint written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. driver and owner raised preliminary objection that accident had not been caused due to the negligence of respondent no. 1 and the same was caused due to the negligence of petitioner.
They claimed that the petitioner was hit by some other vehicle and offending vehicle had been falsely implicated by him in the present case.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 27.08.2019 by my Ld. Predecessor:
1.

Whether the injured Sunil @ Sonu @ Mohit suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 28.04.2019 at about 11:15 am at main K.N.K. Marg, near MC Primary School, Dwarkadhish, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS. KNK Marg due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver Sh.
Sudhir Garg who was driving the vehicle bearing registration no. DL8CAT6309, owned by Sh Govind Garg?OPP.
2.
Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 5.
In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined two witnesses i.e. himself as PW1 and PW2 Dr. Pankaj Bansal and his evidence was closed vide order dated 31.08.2022.

On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by any of the respondents and RE was closed vide order dated 29.10.2022.
6.

Before proceeding further, it may be noted that vide order dated 24.03.2021 passed by my Ld.
Predecessor, it was directed that the petitioner shall not be entitled to any interest from 24.03.2021 till further orders as he had failed to lead his evidence despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities.
Record shows that PE was concluded on 31.08.2022.
Thus, his right to claim interest has been curtailed from 24.03.2021 till 31.08.2022.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments addressed by ld counsels for the parties.
I have also gone through the record.

My findings on the issues are as under:
8. For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW1 Sh. Mohit Sagar @ Sunil @ Sonu (injured himself) is relevant.
In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), PW1 has deposed on the lines of averments made in the DAR.

He has relied upon the following documents: MACP No. 552/19;
FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 S.No.

Description of documents Remarks 1. Original discharge slips Ex PW1/1(colly) & Ex. PW1/2(colly)
2. Original OPD Cards and Ex. PW1/3(colly) medical reports 3.
Medical Bills Ex. PW1/4(colly)
4. Copy of his Aadhaar Card Ex. PW1/5 5. Copy of his driving licence Ex. PW1/6 6.
DAR Ex
. PW1/7(colly)
9. During his cross examination on behalf of driver and owner, he denied the suggestion that accident had taken place due to his fault and negligence.

10. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of crossexamination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely about the accident.
Moreover, FIR No. 161/19 (which is part of DAR) is shown to have been registered on the statement of petitioner himself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 11.

The very fact that respondent no. 1 was chargesheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Same also points out towards the fact that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Furthermore, said FIR is shown to have been registered on 28.04.2019 i.e. on the date of accident itself.
Thus, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Not only this, the respondent no. 1 was a material witness, who could have thrown light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box, during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

13. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at SRHC Hospital,
Delhi shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 28.04.2019 with alleged history of RTA.

On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned MACP No.
552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.

14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 28.04.2019 at about 11:15 am at K.N.K. Marg, near M.C. Primary School, Dwarkadhish, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE NO. 2.
15. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 16.

The petitioner deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was removed to BSA Hospital, Rohini, MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD:
15.02.2023 Delhi where he was medically examined and thereafter, on 29.04.2019, he was shifted to Lok Nayak Hospital, Jawahar Lal Nehru Marg, New Delhi, where he was operated and discharged on 02.06.2019.

He deposed that he had spent total sum of Rs. 38,634/ on his treatment.

For this, he has relied upon medical bills Ex.
PW1/4(colly).
None of the respondents crossexamined this witness on this aspect at all despite grant of opportunity.
17. It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills(Ex. PW1/4 colly) to the tune of Rs. 38,634/.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.

sentences.text: LOSS OF INCOME 18.

The petitioner has categorically deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he aged about 31 years was self employed as Motor Mechanic and earning Rs. 22,000/ per month at the time of accident.

He further deposed that due to the injuries suffered by him in the MACP No.
552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 accident, he could not work for about 1 years and thus, suffered loss of of income.

During his crossexamination on behalf of respondents,
he deposed that at the time of accident, he was working as Motor Mechanic and earning Rs.
22,000/ per month.

He further deposed that he was residing on rent and was paying rent of Rs.
4,000/ per month (excluding water and electricity bill) at that time.
He further deposed that his three children were studying in private schools and he was paying monthly tuition fee in the school @ Rs. 2,400/ of all his children.

He further deposed that he was also paying private tuition fee @
Rs. 650/ per month of all his three children.
He deposed that the monthly rent of his tenanted shop was Rs. 9,000/ and he had been working in the said shop for the last about seven years.
He denied the suggestion that he was not earning Rs. 22,000/ per month at the time of accident.
He further denied the suggestion that he had been working as an employee in the said shop.

19. The medical treatment record i.e. Discharge Summary (Ex. PW1/1) of Lok Nayak Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that he was admitted in the said hospital on 29.04.2019 and discharged on 02.06.2019.
As per the said record, the petitioner had sustained open fracture SOH (right side) with fracture NOF(right side) with SOH(right side) grade IIIB.

The second Discharge Summary (Ex. PW1/2) of Lok Nayak Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that he was again admitted in the said hospital on 28.12.2019 and discharged on 11.01.2020.

As per the said record, the case of the petitioner was of MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS.
K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 fracture SOH(right) nonunion with post op fracture NOF and fracture SOF with penal.
20.
The medical treatment record filed by the petitioner reveals that he had taken treatment from Lok Nayak Hospital.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries as mentioned above due to the accident.
Moreover, the treatment of petitioner continued for about 8 months.
This fact is duly corroborated by the medical treatment record i.e. Discharge Summaries of Lok Nayak Hospital filed by the petitioner.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 10 months or so.
21. During the course of arguments, Ld. counsel for injured vehemently argued that income of petitioner should be taken as Rs. 22,000/per month for computation of his income under this head.
It is further argued that petitioner was self employed and was doing the work of Motor Mechanic in his tenanted shop at the time of accident.

It may be noted here that during the cross examination of petitioner by the Ld. Counsel for respondents, he deposed that he was residing in a tenanted house at the monthly rent of Rs. 4,000/ at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he was paying monthly fee of Rs. 2,400/ of all of his three children.

He further deposed that he was Sh. Sunil @ Sonu @ Mohit vs Sh. Sudhir Garg on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153311830/

sentences.text: He also deposed that he was MACP No. 552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 working on his tenanted shop as motor mechanic at a monthly rent of Rs. 9,000/.

It is pertinent to mention here that Ld. Counsel for respondents nowhere given the suggestion to the petitioner while conducting his cross examination that the aforesaid amounts were not being spent by him monthly under the aforesaid heads which persuades this Tribunal to accept the aforesaid amount as genuine.
For the rough idea of income of petitioner, if we add up the aforesaid amounts that would comes out to be more than Rs. 22,000/ per month.

Thus, keeping in view the expenses used to be incurred by him at the time of accident, I am in agreement with the submission made by Ld. Counsel for petitioner that monthly income of petitioner should be taken as Rs. 22,000/.

Though, there is no direct evidence available qua the income of petitioner, however, from the cross examination of petitioner conducted on behalf of driver and registered owner, there is no doubt that petitioner was earning atleast Rs. 22,000/ per month.
Preserving the existing standard of living by the petitioner is a fundamental endeavour of motor accident compensation law.
Accordingly, the monthly income of petitioner as on the date and time of accident is taken as Rs. 22,000/.

PAIN AND SUFFERING 22.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors."
passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under: " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the compensation is required to be paid for pain and suffering an attempt must be made to award compensation which may have some objective relation with the pain and suffering underwent by the victim.

For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment".
23.
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 13% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings and mental shock on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 13% in relation to his right lower limb.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.
In view of the nature of injuries suffered by him, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/ towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 25.
In his evidence, the petitioner has deposed that he had spent a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/ on special diet, Rs. 50,000/ on conveyance and Rs. 80,000/ on attendant.
The petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount spent by him under the aforesaid heads.

At the same time,
it cannot be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 13% in relation to his right lower limb.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up MACP No.
552/19; FIR No. 161/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 15.02.2023 during the period of his medical treatment.

He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family,
to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.
In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 20,000/ for special diet, Rs. 10,000/ each for conveyance and attendant charges to the petitioner.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME 26.
As already stated above, the petitioner is shown to have sustained 13% permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.

28. The disability certificate (Ex. PW2/1) of injured would reveal that he had suffered 13%
permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
The petitioner in the present case was stated to be doing the work of Motor Mechanic at the time of accident.
It is quite obvious that for a Motor Mechanic, proper movement of all the limbs is very necessary.
A profile of Motor Mechanic necessarily includes site visits etc and thus, lower limbs plays an important role in the said profession.

Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case including the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner as well as the disability suffered by him, his functional disability is taken as 13% with regard to whole body.
(Reliance placed on "Arjun & Ors., Vs. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.", MAC Appeal No. 223/16, decided on 04.01.2018, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Malti Devi & Ors., in MAC.

Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Offending vehicle is uninsured.

Respondent no. 1 being principal tortfeasor and respondent no. 2 being owner of the offending vehicle and thus, vicariously liable for the acts of principal tortfeasor, are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.facts:
DAR filed by police, was treated as claim petition under Section 166(4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and the same was found uninsured during the period in question.
3. In their joint written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e. driver and owner raised preliminary objection that accident had not been caused due to the negligence of respondent no. 1 and the same was caused due to the negligence of petitioner.
They claimed that the petitioner was hit by some other vehicle and offending vehicle had been falsely implicated by him in the present case.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the DAR and prayed for its dismissal.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries as mentioned above due to the accident.
Moreover, the treatment of petitioner continued for about 8 months.
This fact is duly corroborated by the medical treatment record i.e. Discharge Summaries of Lok Nayak Hospital filed by the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Moreover, FIR No. 161/19 (which is part of DAR) is shown to have been registered on the statement of petitioner himself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
The very fact that respondent no. 1 was chargesheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Furthermore, said FIR is shown to have been registered on 28.04.2019 i.e. on the date of accident itself.
Thus, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.
Not only this, the respondent no. 1 was a material witness, who could have thrown light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box, during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
Preserving the existing standard of living by the petitioner is a fundamental endeavour of motor accident compensation law.
I am supported in my aforesaid view by the decision(s) rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case reported as,
"MAC.APP.No.274/2010", titled as, "New India Assurance Company Limited V/s Suminder Kaur &
Ors." (DOD: 28.04.2010), MAC APP.No.646648/2005, titled as, "Surinder Kaur Chhabra & Ors.
V/s Kusum & Ors.", (DOD: 05.12.2012) and titled as, "Smt. Asha Gupta V/s Ramji Lal & Ors.",
(DOD: 20.01.2003).
Keeping in view the medical treatment record of petitioner available on record and the nature of injuries suffered by him, I hereby award a sum of Rs. 75,000/ towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
28. The disability certificate (Ex. PW2/1) of injured would reveal that he had suffered 13%
permanent disability in relation to his right lower limb.
The petitioner in the present case was stated to be doing the work of Motor Mechanic at the time of accident.
It is quite obvious that for a Motor Mechanic, proper movement of all the limbs is very necessary.
A profile of Motor Mechanic necessarily includes site visits etc and thus, lower limbs plays an important role in the said profession.
Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case including the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner as well as the disability suffered by him, his functional disability is taken as 13% with regard to whole body.
opennyai_summary.issue:
14. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 28.04.2019 at about 11:15 am at K.N.K. Marg, near M.C. Primary School, Dwarkadhish, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
